messages:
devon: Heads up — strange dup POST issue in our Kotlin SDK on some Android 13 devices. Using Retrofit + a custom suspend adapter; sometimes a single user action produces two POSTs and duplicate side effects. Repro on Pixel 8 emulator and a couple of customer devices. Anyone seen this pattern?

kevin: Hmm. Do you have OkHttp/Retrofit versions? Any logs that show two full request cycles?

devon: OkHttp 4.11.0, Retrofit 2.9, custom suspend CallAdapterFactory. Log shows two complete POST send/response cycles back-to-back: 
```
I/OkHttp: --> POST https://api.prod.example.com/v1/submit
I/OkHttp: --> END POST (145-byte body)
I/OkHttp: <-- 500 Internal Server Error https://api.prod.example.com/v1/submit (340ms)
I/OkHttp: --> POST https://api.prod.example.com/v1/submit
I/OkHttp: --> END POST (145-byte body)
I/OkHttp: <-- 200 OK https://api.prod.example.com/v1/submit (18ms)
```

maria: That looks like the Call was executed twice. Are you ever reusing the same Call instance or closing over it in the adapter? Retrofit should normally create a new Call for each service method invocation but a buggy adapter can capture the original call reference.

devon: Adapter is small; basically converts Call<T> -> suspend function with suspendCoroutine + call.enqueue. Simplified: 
```
class SuspendCallAdapterFactory: CallAdapter.Factory() {
  override fun get(...): CallAdapter<*, *>? {
    return object: CallAdapter<Any, Any> {
      override fun adapt(call: Call<Any>): Any {
        return suspendCoroutine { cont ->
          call.enqueue(object: Callback<Any> { ... onResponse -> cont.resume(response.body()) ... })
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

sam: There it is — adapter uses the passed-in call directly. If a coroutine is cancelled and then retried, you might end up enqueuing the same Call more than once (or reusing it across coroutine instances). Use call.clone() to ensure a fresh Call per adapt invocation and hook cancellation to cancel the cloned call.

maria: Also make sure to wire cont.invokeOnCancellation { cloned.cancel() } so slow network + job cancellation doesn't leak. We hit a similar duplication years ago when a token refresh triggered coroutine restart.

devon: Implemented clone + cancellation handling: 
```
val fresh = call.clone()
return suspendCancellableCoroutine { cont ->
  cont.invokeOnCancellation { fresh.cancel() }
  fresh.enqueue(object: Callback<T> { ... })
}
```

kevin: Nice. Can you confirm with a stress run? Also add a small integration test with a fake OkHttp client that just records request counts. If flaky, add server-side idempotency key as a belt-and-suspenders mitigation.

devon: Ran 1k runs on Pixel 8 emulator with orientation changes and backgrounding toggles: duplicates gone. Adding tests and a sample-app demo in a PR.

maria: Recommend adding a short note to devdocs: "Retrofit suspend adapters must clone Call and support cancellation to avoid duplicate execution on coroutine restarts or Android lifecycle events." Save people some debugging time.

ci-bot: CI for branch `fix/suspend-adapter-clone` completed: all checks passed.

sam: Also sanity-check OkHttp connection reuse and interceptors — if an interceptor mutates request bodies or streaming bodies, cloning semantics matter. But clone() is the right fix here.

devon: Thanks all. I'll push the PR with tests and docs. Will also add a tiny sample-app scenario under devex/samples to reproduce locally. Closing the issue after merge. :tada:
